description:
1. Create a folder named "temp_checks" and record the initial environment state into "temp_checks/state.log".
2. Recursively enumerate all entries under /working and save the raw listing to "temp_checks/raw_listing.txt".
3. From "temp_checks/raw_listing.txt", extract paths whose final path component is exactly "workspace" and save them to "temp_checks/candidates.txt".
4. For each path listed in "temp_checks/candidates.txt", verify its file type and write those confirmed to be regular files into "temp_checks/regular_candidates.txt".
5. Normalize and deduplicate the entries in "temp_checks/regular_candidates.txt" and save the unique canonical paths to "temp_checks/regular_unique.txt".
6. Compare the counts and contents between "temp_checks/candidates.txt" and "temp_checks/regular_unique.txt" and log any discrepancies to "temp_checks/consistency.log".
7. Create a one-line summary file "temp_checks/result_prepare.txt" containing "found" if "temp_checks/regular_unique.txt" is non-empty or "not_found" if it is empty, leaving the final yes/no decision to be made from that summary.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "tmp_check" in the current environment to hold all intermediate artifacts and ensure it is empty.  
2. Obtain a recursive listing of the /working path and save the raw listing to "tmp_check/listing.raw".  
3. From "tmp_check/listing.raw", extract all paths whose final component is exactly "workspace" and save those paths to "tmp_check/candidates.txt".  
4. For each path listed in "tmp_check/candidates.txt", retrieve and record its file type metadata (e.g., regular file, directory, symlink) alongside the path into "tmp_check/metadata.txt".  
5. From "tmp_check/metadata.txt", filter and write only the paths confirmed to be regular files into "tmp_check/regular_matches.txt".  
6. Remove any temporary entries in "tmp_check" that are not needed for the final presence check, preserving only "tmp_check/regular_matches.txt" and a short provenance file "tmp_check/provenance.txt" that documents the steps taken.  
7. Confirm that "tmp_check/regular_matches.txt" is present and readable and prepare the environment so a single final presence check can read that file and output "yes" if it is non-empty or "no" if it is empty.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && mkdir /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named '/working/temp_workspace' to hold intermediate artifacts and record that path for later steps.
2. Recursively enumerate all entries under '/working' and save the raw listing to '/working/temp_workspace/raw_listing.txt'.
3. From raw_listing.txt, filter the entries to include only regular files (exclude directories and special files) and save those paths to '/working/temp_workspace/regular_files.txt'.
4. Normalize and deduplicate the regular file paths, then sort them and save the result to '/working/temp_workspace/normalized_files.txt'.
5. Extract from normalized_files.txt any entries whose filename (basename) equals 'workspace' and write those full paths to '/working/temp_workspace/matches.txt'.
6. Re-verify that each path in matches.txt still refers to a regular file and write a single flag file '/working/temp_workspace/present.flag' containing "true" if any verified matches exist, otherwise "false".
7. Prepare a one-line staged result file '/working/temp_workspace/result_ready.txt' that will contain "yes" if present.flag is "true" or "no" if present.flag is "false", leaving the actual printing of that line for the final step.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_checks" to hold all intermediate artifacts for the verification process.
2. Obtain a recursive listing of /working and save the result to "temp_checks/initial_listing.txt".
3. Extract from "temp_checks/initial_listing.txt" every entry whose final component is exactly "workspace" and save those lines to "temp_checks/matches_raw.txt".
4. For each path in "temp_checks/matches_raw.txt", determine whether that path refers to a regular file (not a directory or link) and append the path plus its type to "temp_checks/matches_checked.txt".
5. Normalize the paths in "temp_checks/matches_checked.txt", remove duplicate entries, and save the cleaned list to "temp_checks/matches_normalized.txt".
6. Inspect "temp_checks/matches_normalized.txt" and write a single state file "temp_checks/found_regular_file.flag" set to "true" if any entry is a regular file, otherwise set it to "false".
7. Produce a short summary in "temp_checks/summary.txt" that references "temp_checks/found_regular_file.flag" and "temp_checks/matches_normalized.txt", making the prepared state ready for the final decision.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/workspace
